name: wait-without-a-predicate
why: wait(lock) with no predicate: it waits even if the queue was already closed or non-empty (a lost wake-up).

name: push-does-not-wake-a-consumer
why: a consumer that waits in pop() is never told that a value arrived.

edits.old:
lock.unlock();  // do not wake a thread that would immediately block on our mutex
        not_empty_.notify_one();

name: pop-does-not-wake-a-producer
why: a producer that waits for room is never told that room appeared.

name: close-does-not-wake-anybody
why: threads that wait in push or pop are never told that the queue is closed.

edits.old:
not_full_.notify_all();   // every waiting producer must see that the queue is closed...
        not_empty_.notify_all();  // ...and so must every waiting consumer

name: close-wakes-only-one-consumer
why: notify_one instead of notify_all: with three waiting consumers, two sleep for ever.

edits.old: not_empty_.notify_all();  // ...and so must every waiting consumer

name: push-ignores-the-capacity
why: push never waits for room: the queue grows past its capacity.

name: capacity-off-by-one
why: one value too many fits (<= instead of <).

name: pop-does-not-wait
why: pop returns an empty result at once when there is nothing (it behaves like try_pop).

edits.old:
not_empty_.wait(lock, [this] { return closed_ || !items_.empty(); });
        if (items_.empty()) return std::nullopt;  // closed, and nothing left

name: push-after-close-is-accepted
why: the value is queued even though the queue is closed.

name: close-throws-the-queued-values-away
why: close() empties the queue: values that were queued are lost.

name: size-without-the-lock
why: size() reads the deque while other threads change it: a data race.

name: busy-waiting-consumer
why: pop spins (unlock, yield, lock) instead of waiting on the condition variable: it works, and burns the processor.

edits.old:
not_empty_.wait(lock, [this] { return closed_ || !items_.empty(); });
        if (items_.empty()) return std::nullopt;  // closed, and nothing left
